summary: David, confronted by prophet Nathan after adultery with Bathsheba and arranging Uriah's death, prays for mercy: blot out transgressions, wash, cleanse, create clean heart, do not take Holy Spirit, restore joy, then I will teach. Ends asking God to do good to Zion and accept sacrifices of righteous heart not just ritual.
whyItMatters: Classic penitential psalm — model for confession without excuses. Shows biblical view: sin is against God chiefly, need is not just forgiveness but new heart, and restoration leads to teaching others. Used in Lent, confession liturgies.

context.author: David, after 2 Samuel 11-12
context.setting: After being confronted about adultery and murder, palace

outline.heading: Appeal to mercy — blot, wash, cleanse
Acknowledgment — against you only have I sinned, truth in inward parts
Prayer for inner renewal — purge hyssop, create clean heart, restore Spirit and joy
Vow to teach transgressors and praise
Sacrifices — not burnt offering but broken spirit

keyVerses.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
keyVerses.why: Most quoted — creation language (bara, same as Genesis 1) for inner renewal, not just repair.

keyVerses.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.
keyVerses.why: Defines acceptable sacrifice after moral failure.

keyVerses.text: Against you, and you only, I have sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight, so you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge.
keyVerses.why: Shocking claim after harming Uriah and Bathsheba — means sin's core is against God.

questions.question: Why does David say 'Against you only have I sinned' when he clearly sinned against Bathsheba and Uriah?
questions.answer: He doesn't deny harm to them — narrative in 2 Samuel shows he did. But he says ultimate offense is against God, whose law and trust he violated. Like embezzling from company — you harm company and founder. Recognizing vertical dimension prevents just interpersonal apology without dealing with God.

questions.question: What does 'Create in me a clean heart' mean? Why 'create' not 'fix'?
questions.answer: Hebrew bara — create, same verb as Genesis 1:1. David asks not for renovation but new creation. Broken heart can't self-repair; needs divine act. Renew a right (steadfast) spirit — stable, not fickle. Implies need beyond forgiveness: new inner orientation.

questions.question: What does 'purge me with hyssop' mean?
questions.answer: Hyssop branch used to sprinkle blood on Passover doorposts and to cleanse lepers and houses (Leviticus 14). Image is ritual cleansing for impurity. David feels stained, needs deep cleansing beyond surface wash — hyssop evokes blood and purification rites.

questions.question: How can David be forgiven after adultery and murder? Isn't that too easy?
questions.answer: Psalm doesn't minimize sin — calls it transgression, iniquity, sin, bloodguilt. But appeals to God's hesed (steadfast love) and compassion, not own merit. Shows biblical pattern: forgiveness is costly (later Christians see cross as cost), not cheap, but possible because God desires broken spirit over perfect record. Consequences remain (child dies, family strife in narrative).

questions.question: What does 'do not take your Holy Spirit from me' mean? Can Spirit be lost?
questions.answer: In Old Testament, Spirit comes upon leaders for task (Saul lost Spirit in 1 Samuel 16). David saw Saul lose kingship and Spirit, fears same. In New Testament, Spirit given as indwelling for all believers. David's prayer is for continued presence and empowerment, not just feeling. Restore joy of salvation (v12) — loss of joy, not just status, is pain of sin.

questions.question: Why does it end with building walls of Jerusalem and sacrifices?
questions.answer: Verses 18-19 may be later addition after exile, or David as king praying for city's welfare after his personal sin affected community. Point: personal restoration leads to communal good — do good to Zion. God desires not just ritual (burnt offering) but broken heart; then ritual has meaning.

glossary.def: Small plant used as brush to sprinkle blood/water for cleansing rituals.
Hebrew verb used only for divine creating, not human making — new creation, not repair.
Crushed, broken, like pulverized — heart broken over sin, not just sorry caught.
